decisions.reason: Despite its disappearance from later website snapshots, this multi-model underground loader line sits close to the firm's stated strategic direction and embodies high sunk engineering and reputational commitment, so management would still be inclined to continue and blame weak uptake on long mining sales cycles and recent disruptions.

The underground dump truck line is likewise a capital-intensive, strategically central launch whose disappointing visibility can still be framed as temporary market timing rather than definitive failure, making continued commitment more likely than withdrawal.

As a single construction-site dumper introduced only in 2019, it appears less distinctive and less central than the underground and lift lines, so with limited visible follow-through management would be more willing by 2022 to stop it and reallocate resources.

This inclined furniture lift was launched as a product line with its own page, signaling visible commitment and a service-based niche fit with the firm's lifting capabilities, which under escalation of commitment supports keeping it unless failure is unmistakable.

The inclined building material lift line matches the firm's construction and material-handling positioning and involved a public multi-model rollout, so management would be inclined to persist and attribute any shortfall to temporary construction-market conditions.

The truck-mounted inclined furniture lift is a narrower single product and therefore easier to discontinue than the broader lift lines, especially if demand has not clearly justified the added complexity and vehicle-specific commitment.
